newsitem.title: GERMANY: German paper's leading economic indicator dips.
newsitem.headline: German paper's leading economic indicator dips.

text.p: The Handelsblatt daily said on Friday that its leading indicator for the German economy dipped in January but still pointed to a continuation of the recovery which began during 1996.
The leading indicator showed a rise of 1.6 percent in January after 1.7 percent in December -- when the figure was revised up slightly following strong Christmas retail sales.
Handelsblatt said that the slight fall in its leading indicator for January stemmed from the gloomier outlook among manufacturers in western Germany.

"It is still too early to talk about a leap forward in the domestic economy," the newspaper commented. "But, bearing in mind steeply rising exports...the spark should jump to the domestic cycle in the foreseeable future."

The leading indicator is based on a weighted combination of latest west German industrial and building orders, national retail sales, the Ifo business confidence survey and the difference between long- and short-term interest rates.
The indicator is intended to predict fluctuations in gross domestic product a quarter-year in advance.
